reader.requirement: At --std 85 a figurative constant other than ALL literal (ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES, SPACE/SPACES, HIGH-VALUE(S), LOW-VALUE(S), QUOTE(S), a symbolic-character, each with or without the redundant word ALL) that is not associated with a data item, as in DISPLAY, STOP literal, STRING (sending operand or delimiter) and UNSTRING (delimiter), must stand for exactly one character.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(StopLiteralRemoved2002): the STOP literal SR1/SR3 screens run only where STOP literal exists (1985); later editions refuse the statement (COBOL0902 from VersionConformancePass)
ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(StopLiteralRemoved2002): a STOP word naming no symbolic-character is refused by name (COBOL7558) at 1985 only

reader.edition-search: grep for CobolVersion/Edition/IsAtLeast/DialectBehavior in OperandText.cs and FigurativeConstants.cs: none; the DISPLAY/STRING/UNSTRING one-character rendering (OperandText.AsString's BoundFigurative arm: new string(fill, 1)) is edition-blind; only the STOP path consults the edition, through the StopLiteralRemoved2002 construct row.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the STOP literal statement exists only at 1985 (removed by 2002), so the STOP arm of the rule is 1985's alone; the DISPLAY/STRING/UNSTRING one-character length is the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf02_01 covers DISPLAY ZERO/SPACE/QUOTES, STRING SPACES/ZEROS as senders and UNSTRING DELIMITED BY SPACES; pb5809 covers STOP symbolic-character. Not exercised there: HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE, the redundant ALL before a non-literal figurative, a symbolic-character in DISPLAY/STRING, STRING delimiters, UNSTRING delimiters other than SPACE, STOP with a keyword figurative

probes.expected: §1985:VI.6.25.3 SR1 forbids a figurative that begins with ALL in STRING (refusal correct; message cites §2023:14.9.43.3 SR2 at --std 85)

reader.notes: Every keyword figurative binds to a BoundFigurative (the word ALL dropped), a symbolic-character to a one-character BoundAllLiteral, and OperandText.AsString renders a BoundFigurative in a string position as new string(fill, 1); STOP folds the figurative to its one character (ConcatFolder.FigurativeChar) or the symbolic value. All four statements named by the rule were probed and give one character. Side observation: the STRING ALL-figurative refusal at --std 85 cites §2023:14.9.43.3 SR2 rather than §1985:VI.6.25.3 SR1 (diagnostic citation only).

refuter.evidence: fg2.cob under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV (ALPHABET REV IS "Z" THRU "A"). STRING HIGH-VALUES LOW-VALUES ZERO advances the pointer by 3 (H1 P=04; od -c shows one U+FFFF, then 'Z' as the lowest character of the program sequence, then '0'). DISPLAY HIGH-VALUE / LOW-VALUE shows one character each. UNSTRING DELIMITED BY symbolic STAR gives [AB][CD][  ][EF] T=4, and with ALL STAR [AB][CD][EF] T=3. STRING 'ABC' DELIMITED BY LOW-VALUE and 'XAY' DELIMITED BY HIGH-VALUE gives P=07. STRING SPACE DELIMITED BY SPACE / ZERO DELIMITED BY QUOTE / STAR gives [0*] P=03. STOP HIGH-VALUE and STOP STAR each write one character and continue. STRING ALL ZERO was refused COBOL1757, matching the 1985 STRING SR1 bar on ALL. All of this agrees with the one-character rule. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 GRL2.2.
